title: RESTWS-1058: Use Authorize for masking resources
body:
https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/RESTWS-1058

Core 3.0 adds `DomainObjectAuthorizationRule` (openmrs/openmrs-core#6668), which lets a module decide **per object** — not per privilege — who may read a given record: this patient is on a restricted ward, that observation belongs to a trial the current user is not on.

RESTWS needs to use these rules (if deployed by an implementation) for masking referenced resources.

title: RESTWS-1056: Translate AccessDeniedException to the same 401/403 handling as APIAuthenticationException
body:
## Summary
- `openmrs-core` [TRUNK-6799](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core/pull/6544) (merged) introduces Spring Security. A denied privilege check now surfaces as `org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException` - `@PreAuthorize` throws the `AuthorizationDeniedException` subclass, `@Authorized` throws it too, and `APIAuthenticationException` is deprecated with "catch and throw Spring Security's `AccessDeniedException` instead".
- `BaseRestController` only recognized `APIAuthenticationException`, so a denial came back as a 500 with an ERROR stack trace instead of the expected 401 (not logged in) / 403 (logged in, lacking privilege).
- Two changes, both needed:
  - `AccessDeniedException` goes on `apiAuthenticationExceptionHandler`'s own `@ExceptionHandler`, next to `APIAuthenticationException`. Spring picks the handler mapped to the closest exception type, so without this a subclass declaring a broader handler of its own never reaches the catch-all - Bahmni appointments' `AppointmentUnavailabilityController` maps `RuntimeException` to a 400, and answered denials with 400 plus a stack trace.
  - A `RestUtil.hasCause(ex, AccessDeniedException.class)` branch in the `Exception` catch-all, for denials wrapped in another exception. Spring only consults the cause chain when no handler matches the exception itself, and the catch-all always matches.
- Matching on the supertype covers `AuthorizationDeniedException` as well, since `RestUtil.hasCause` uses `ExceptionUtils.indexOfType`.
- No pom change: with core#6544, `openmrs-api` declares `spring-security-core` at compile scope, so it reaches this module as provided the same way `spring-security-crypto` already does. An earlier revision pinned it explicitly; that was dropped, which also makes CI hold the ordering behind core.

## Upgrade note
A module controller that maps `AccessDeniedException` under a method name of its own now fails with "Ambiguous @ExceptionHandler method mapped" on the first exception that controller handles. Override `apiAuthenticationExceptionHandler` to customize the response instead. This is noted in the method's javadoc.

## Test plan
- [x] `BaseRestControllerTest` - 14/14 pass (`mvn -pl omod -am test -Dtest=BaseRestControllerTest`), including:
  - `handleException` with a plain `AccessDeniedException` and with `AuthorizationDeniedException`, logged in and logged out.
  - Two MockMvc tests resolving the exception through a `BaseRestController` subclass that maps `RuntimeException` to a 400, which pin the `@ExceptionHandler` mapping - they fail with 400 without it.
- [x] Verified on core 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT build 435: `GET /ws/rest/v1/appointmentUnavailability` answered anonymous, unprivileged and wrong-password callers with 400 before this PR, and 401, 403, 401 after.

## Known CI failures, not caused by this PR
Both fail the same way on this branch's base against core 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT build 435:
- `ChangePasswordController1_8Test.testUserChangeOtherUsersPasswordWithOutPrivilege` expects `APIAuthenticationException` ([TRUNK-6823](https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/TRUNK-6823)).
- `ConversionUtil1_9Test.convertToRepresentation_shouldNotLeakPatientDataThroughVisitCustomRepresentation` hits openmrs/openmrs-core#6669, fixed by openmrs/openmrs-core#6671.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

[TRUNK-6823]: https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/TRUNK-6823?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

title: RESTWS-1052: Apply order arbitration to class-based resource lookup
body:
## Summary
`RestServiceImpl.initializeResources()` builds two lookup maps: `resourceDefinitionsByNames` (order-arbitrated on name collisions) and `resourcesBySupportedClasses` (no arbitration at all — last one scanned wins, regardless of `order`).

Because `RestService.getResourceBySupportedClass(Class)` and `ConversionUtil.getConverter(Class)` (which delegates to it) both read from `resourcesBySupportedClasses`, a resource can be silently and non-deterministically replaced by an unrelated, differently-named resource from another module that happens to support the same domain class — even when the replaced resource has a better `order` and would win a same-name comparison. Core's own `MainResourceController.retrieve()` resolves by name, so it's unaffected; custom code that resolves by class is exposed.

This fix applies the same `order`-based arbitration already used for `resourceDefinitionsByNames` to `resourcesBySupportedClasses`.

Fixes RESTWS-1052.

## Test plan
- Added `getResourceBySupportedClass_shouldNotBeClobberedByADifferentlyNamedResourceWithAWorseOrder` and `getResourceByName_shouldReturnResourceThatLostTheBySupportedClassLookup` to `RestServiceImplTest`, using a new fixture `AnimalWithHigherOrderResource_1_9`.
- Verified manually (via `git stash`) that the first new test fails without this fix and passes with it.
- Full `omod` test suite passes (55/55 in `RestServiceImplTest`).

title: RESTWS-1049: Fix broken tests in master branch
body:
<!--- Add a pull request title above in this format -->
<!--- real example: 'RESTWS-738 Remove concept property setters from ObsResource classes' -->
<!--- 'RESTWS-JiraIssueNumber JiraIssueTitle' -->
## Description of what I changed
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->

Upstream core changes broke some of the tests in the master branch for the REST module here. See failing tests [here](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest/actions/runs/32291007969/job/96191710037). See summary by Claude below. Note that I plan to either remove `swagger-core:1.6.2` or upgrade it to a significantly more recent version soon, so the fix to problem 1 will likely change later. 

Also, if `master` branch in `openmrs-core` is stable enough, we should consider adding a Github action there to build against this module.

Summary by Claude:

**Problem 1 (guava).** openmrs-core `c4aca3af4` (#6233) added `OutboxEventRegistry`, a Spring bean
whose constructor calls `CacheBuilder.expireAfterWrite(Duration.ofMinutes(10))` — an overload that
exists only in the **jre** flavor of Guava, which core manages. But `omod-common` was resolving
`guava:27.0.1-android` via `io.swagger:swagger-core:1.6.2`, which wins Maven's nearest-declaration
mediation. Since the bean loads with every Spring context, all 112 context-sensitive tests in the
module failed at once with `NoSuchMethodError`. Latent defect here, not an upstream regression.
**Fix:** pin `guava:33.7.0-jre` in the root pom's `dependencyManagement`; packaging unchanged.

**Problem 2 (fixtures).** openmrs-core `1b5421a9a` (TRUNK-6712, #6383) added `RolePrivilegeCache` and
rewrote `UserContext.hasPrivilege` — role privileges now come from a cache populated by a daemon
thread that reloads the role from the DB and fails closed if absent, where the old path walked the
in-memory role graph. Both fixtures depended on that removed behaviour: one attached a role purely in
memory, the other saved one inside the test's rolled-back transaction. **Fix:** core's own adaptation
pattern from that commit — `Context.addProxyPrivilege(...)` in try/finally. Test-only.

title: RESTWS-1040: Add TypedSimpleObject<T> class
body:
## Description of what I changed

Adds `TypedSimpleObject<T>` (extends `SimpleObject`) as the foundation for RESTWS-1040, and migrates a small proof-of-concept batch of 5 resource classes from `new SimpleObject()` to `new TypedSimpleObject<>()` at their construction sites, ahead of a larger rollout across the rest of the codebase.

`TypedSimpleObject<T>` extends `SimpleObject` (not `LinkedHashMap` directly) per discussion with @chibongho — this preserves backward compatibility for modules relying on `SimpleObject` while migrating to REST 4.x. The `<T>` generic is currently unused (`TypedSimpleObject<?>`) as an interim step; follow-up tickets will fill in concrete types.

Migrated classes: `SystemInformationResource1_8`, `ServerLogResource1_8`, `ServerLogResource2_4`, `OrderEntryConfigResource1_10`, `ObsResource1_8`.

Method return type signatures were intentionally left as `SimpleObject` (constrained by the `Listable` interface contract) — since `TypedSimpleObject` extends `SimpleObject`, assignment compatibility is preserved and callers are unaffected. Only local variable declarations and construction sites were changed.

This is a small PoC batch to validate the migration pattern before scaling to the remaining resource classes.

title: RESTWS-1043: Deprecate Swagger model getters in Resource classes
body:
## Description of what I changed

Marks `getGETModel(rep)`, `getCREATEModel(rep)`, and `getUPDATEModel(rep)` as `@Deprecated` across all Resource classes that implement them, per RESTWS-1043.

These functions currently duplicate (and sometimes contradict) the property-declaring functions (`getRepresentationDescription`, `getCreatableProperties`, `getUpdatableProperties`), which should be the source of truth for Swagger/OpenAPI typings going forward. Since the Swagger JSON has been broken since 3.7 without much attention, it's safe to assume no one depends on the current output.

This is Phase 1: deprecation only, no removal. Two internal callers still reference these methods and will need updates before removal in Phase 2 (tracked separately, blocked on the 4.x branch): `SwaggerSpecificationCreator.java` and `ServerLogActionWrapper2_4.java`.

`@deprecated` version is set to `3.6.0` since this change applies to the 3.x branch.

title: (fix) RESTWS-1027: Re-enable TaskServiceWrapper.runTask()
body:
<!--- Add a pull request title above in this format -->
<!--- real example: 'RESTWS-738 Remove concept property setters from ObsResource classes' -->
<!--- 'RESTWS-JiraIssueNumber JiraIssueTitle' -->
## Description of what I changed
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->
See https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest/pull/731 for context. This PR fixes the TaskServiceWrapper.runTask() after core's migration to using JobRunr. Previously the `runTask()` function runs the task almost immediately. The the new implementation, `Context.getSchedulerService().schedule(taskDefinition)` calls JobRunr's `jobRequestScheduler.enqueue(job)`, which schedule the task for a "fire-and-forget" job; see [javadocs](https://repo.jobrunr.io/javadoc/releases/org/jobrunr/jobrunr-pro/latest/.cache/unpack/org/jobrunr/scheduling/JobRequestScheduler.html#enqueue(org.jobrunr.jobs.lambdas.JobRequest). That said, it's not an immediate run of the job. By default, JobRunr has a polling interval of 15 seconds, See [here](https://javadoc.io/static/org.jobrunr/jobrunr/5.3.2/org/jobrunr/server/BackgroundJobServerConfiguration.html#usingStandardBackgroundJobServerConfiguration()). It doesn't quite match the old behavior of firing right away, but given that it's a scheduled job, it's probably acceptable.

Obs are mostly immutable. When we "edit" an obs, we do so by voiding the current one and creating a new value, with the new obs's `previousVersion` pointing to the old one.  `GET /obs/<uuid>?v=custom:(previousVersion)` allows us to get the previous version. Keeping in line with current behavior of `previousVersion`, I did not put this new property in the full representation.
